🇲🇽🌎 ITALY'S 'INTERNAZIONALE': SHEINBAUM IS THE WORLD'S MOST POPULAR LEFT LEADER

Italy's Internazionale ran a profile of President Sheinbaum under the title "Presidenta de todos," reproducing The Guardian's verdict that she is "by far the most popular left leader in the world," with approval above 70%. As the Americas lurch right, her social-policy agenda stands as the counterweight to Trump — "a source of inspiration for the international left."

PIIE: Ending USMCA could fuel higher US consumer prices
July 8, 2026 | 🟢

The Peterson Institute does the math on killing USMCA: a ~92% tariff pass-through to shoppers and a 2.7% jump in US auto prices. "Punishing" Mexico is really a tax on American wallets.

95.7% of US transport-vehicle imports come from Mexico and Canada — there is no version of this where US consumers don't foot the bill.

• "roughly 92 percent pass-through rate to consumers from tariffs"
• "26.9 percent of all US goods imports came from" Mexico and Canada

LATIN TIMES: Sheinbaum Says Calderón 'Opened the Door' to U.S. Operations on Mexican Soil
July 10, 2026 | 🟢

Latin Times lets Sheinbaum name who actually invited US agents to operate inside Mexico: "Calderón opened the door to U.S. agencies to carry out intelligence, planning and operational activities."

It was the Calderón–García Luna era that normalized US field operations; Sheinbaum now limits foreign agents to intelligence-sharing unless her security cabinet authorizes more.

• "We have a different policy than the one Calderón had."
• "Calderón opened the door to U.S. agencies... in our country."

AL JAZEERA: Sheinbaum takes on cartels, Trump and the legacy of 1968
July 11, 2026 | 🟢

A rare fair longform: Sheinbaum drawn as a "child of 1968," scientist and feminist navigating Trump's pressure — not a narco-state caricature. Her line to Washington stays fixed: "Cooperation, yes; subordination and intervention, no."

Most US outlets default to "failing state"; this one treats her as a serious operator facing genuine dilemmas.

• "Cooperation, yes; subordination and intervention, no."
• "Mexico is nobody's piñata."

🇲🇽📊 MEXICO NOW OWES ITSELF — INTERNAL DEBT CLIMBS FROM 64% TO 78% IN A DECADE

Mexico's internal debt rose from 64% of the total in 2016 to 78% by May 2026, per Hacienda data reported by El Economista, with the domestic balance up 7.8% year-on-year to 14.78 trillion pesos. The logic is sovereignty: borrow in pesos, not dollars, and a weaker peso can no longer automatically inflate what you owe. Less exposure to Washington's rate cycle, less to currency raids — a country financing itself in its own money.

🇲🇽🐄 MEXICO SCALES BACK UP ITS SCREWWORM DEFENSE — 100 MILLION STERILE FLIES A WEEK

Sheinbaum inaugurated a sterile-fly plant in Metapa de Domínguez, Chiapas producing 100 million insects a week to eradicate the screwworm that shut Mexican cattle out of the US market. The sterile insect technique has run out of Chiapas for decades; scaling it back up is how Mexico protects its own herds and food supply. "Animal diseases and food security challenges know no borders," Sheinbaum said.

🇲🇽🏛️ MEXICO HAS CLAWED BACK 3,716 STOLEN ARTIFACTS — 3,369 FROM THE US

Under Sheinbaum, Mexico has recovered 3,716 pieces of looted cultural heritage — 3,369 of them from the United States, the rest from Italy, Canada, France and Spain. Across the Fourth Transformation the total reaches 17,878, which INAH says is 68% more than Calderón and ten times Peña Nieto. And it doesn't end at the border: some pieces go straight back to the communities they were taken from.

🏠🇲🇽 MEXICO CITY HANDS OVER 106 APARTMENTS AT A THIRD OF MARKET PRICE

Mayor Clara Brugada delivered 106 new apartments in Gustavo A. Madero — 60 m², eco-tech, built to international habitability standards — for 424 residents. Cost: about 928,000 pesos a unit, financed by zero-interest public credit scaled to what families can actually repay, against 2–4 million pesos on the open market. It's part of a 200,000-home plan for the term at 9 billion pesos a year. Housing as a right, not a speculative asset.

🇲🇽🚆 THE ISTHMUS CORRIDOR IS MOVING — 3,000 HYUNDAIS, ASIA TO THE US THROUGH MEXICO

The Glovis Cóndor left Masan, South Korea on June 22 carrying 3,000 Hyundai vehicles bound for the US east coast — routed across Mexico's Interoceanic Corridor: ship to Salina Cruz, then 72 hours by rail on double-deck Bi-Max cars to Coatzacoalcos. It's the second auto crossing since the March 2025 pilot moved 900 units. The alternative to the Panama Canal that Washington said would never work is booking cargo.

🇲🇽🌎 MEXICO OPENS THE DOOR TO PERU — ON ITS OWN TERMS

Mexico is ready to reopen relations with Peru, Sheinbaum said, instructing Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco to make contact with president-elect Keiko Fujimori's team. But the reason ties ruptured stands: Mexico granted asylum to ex-PM Betssy Chávez and its position on the 2022 persecution of Pedro Castillo will not change. Diplomacy resumes; the principle doesn't move.
